html:
Oman is the state of the south-east corner of Arabia, on the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. The map shows it from 1530 to today.

Its people mostly follow Ibadi Islam, and from 751 the interior was often ruled by elected Ibadi imams. The Portuguese held Muscat and the coast from 1507 until 1650, when the Yarubid imams drove them out. The Omanis then built a sea empire that took Mombasa and Zanzibar and ruled much of the Swahili coast.

The Al Said family has ruled since about 1744. Said bin Sultan moved his court to Zanzibar, and after his death in 1856 the empire split in two. The Arabian half, Muscat and Oman, was poor and under strong British influence, while the interior imams held out until the 1950s. After the Dhofar rebellion began, Qaboos bin Said took power from his father in 1970, renamed the country the Sultanate of Oman and spent its oil money on roads, schools and hospitals.
